page: The Vultr vc2-2c-2gb is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 shared vCPUs derived from 1 physical core across 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is allocated at 2.0 GB of RAM, offering 1.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX, AVX-512F, and AES instruction support, with an L3 cache size of 16 MB. The instance includes 65 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark outcomes place the instance in low-tier performance brackets overall. CPU throughput via stress-ng registers 1,260.88 for single-core and 2,444.49 for multi-core tests, placing both within the bottom 25%. Synthetic assessment via PassMark yields an overall CPU score of 2,453.98 and a memory score of 938.79, each falling in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 177.44 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached blocks, decreasing to 12.18 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 10.85 GB/sec for writes.

Application-level measurements indicate 1.39 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, alongside 1.72 GB/sec throughput in static web serving benchmarks. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at 20.86 GB/sec, while bzip3 decompression reaches 5.59 GB/sec. Lightweight natural language processing evaluates small 135M parameter models at 115.73 prompt processing tokens per second and 32.64 text generation tokens per second.

The shared CPU allocation and low memory ceiling introduce clear tradeoffs, making the instance ill-suited for heavy computational tasks, large in-memory databases, or multi-tenant production systems. Given its low resource footprint, it functions efficiently as an economical environment for lightweight utility tasks, development prototypes, basic static web serving, DNS hosting, and non-critical background automation.
